unit.title: 2D Shapes
unit.blurb: Equilateral, isosceles and scalene triangles, and lines of symmetry and reflections in patterns.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Identify, describe, classify and sketch isosceles, equilateral and scalene triangles.

O2.t: Identify lines of symmetry in 2D shapes and patterns, and complete symmetrical patterns.

p: An **equilateral** triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles. An **isosceles** triangle has 2 equal sides and 2 equal angles. A **scalene** triangle has no equal sides.
Little marks called **hatch marks** show which sides are equal.
A right-angled triangle can also be isosceles if its two shorter sides are equal.

p: A **line of symmetry** splits a shape into two halves that are mirror images. If you fold along it, the halves match exactly.
A square has 4 lines of symmetry; a rectangle has 2; an equilateral triangle has 3.
To complete a symmetrical pattern, **reflect** each square in the mirror line: it lands the same distance away on the other side.
The diagonals of a rectangle are NOT lines of symmetry: the halves do not match when folded.
